//EXPERIMENT: 2026-10-09: the 10.54 mm2 knobs (cap 20, fanout 16, cell padding 1 site per side, timing-driven global placement, clock on met3-met5, resizer on tt / ff) on the 11.56 mm2 corridor floorplan (3400 x 3400, macro_placement_u2fg.cfg); only the die changes. At 10.54 mm2 the I$ way-1 half-cycle SRAM read path had +0.153 ns at p2 (nom_tt); on that die the same path lost 0.85 ns from p2 to the sign-off max_tt in the earlier run (-0.573 ns). Earlier note of the 10.54 config: SA2 ASIC build, CACHE_CONFIG 1, corridor floorplan corr3400x3100_f220 (DIE_AREA 3400 x 3100, macro_placement_corr3400x3100_f220.cfg). Knobs as config_corr3400x3100_f220_capm20_fo16.json plus three placement / clock-routing knobs aimed at the measured failure of that run (2026-10-08).
//MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT: 8 in the base config; the first design repair (RepairDesignPostGPL) then split 2,520 nets into 14,503 fanout buffers (DM_VC4, corr3400x3400_f220)
//IGNORE_DISCONNECTED_MODULES: The SRAM macro's second port is deliberately unused: csb1 is tied high, addr1 tied low and dout1 left open in axi_ram_32_asic_macro.v. The disconnected-pin checker's own error message says to declare that here when it is intentional. This is a declaration, not a bypass -- the step still runs on every other instance.
//MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: True since 2026-09-25 (FLOW_JOURNAL Incident 61): Magic DRC runs on the real GDS of the standard cells and routing, with the SRAM macros held as LEF abstracts by a local patch to scripts/magic/drc.tcl. DEF mode checked LEF abstracts of the standard cells and reported 4,187 false nwell.4 (0 with real geometry). Macro internals: KLayout DRC on the full GDS, reported separately.
//GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_CAP_PCT: 50 in the base config; 20 = the pre-GRT margin DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_CAP_PCT. With 50, detailed routing of sa2uB needed 54 iterations (70 violations flat from iteration 28 to 44, all in one fanout-buffer cluster)
//SYNTH_OPT_DFF_SAT: openlane-local patch (2026-09-30): one extra OPT round with opt_dff -sat. In DM_VC4 the D-cache way-1 data bank is dead (refill_way can only be 0); Quartus removes it (VC4 = DM = 26 M9K), plain Yosys keeps its flop and four 1 KiB macros (vc4_synth: 12 cache macros). Set in both DSE builds so they are synthesised alike; its effect on DM is measured separately (FLOW_JOURNAL).
//PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT: 42 instead of DM's 55 (2026-10-02): at 55 sa2F_A / vc4F_A stopped with GRT-0118 (SA2 overflow 67,971; routed wire 16.2 m vs DM 8.2 m). 42 is the value of config_R14 / E10 / FINAL3, which E15 raised for DM.
//GRT_ALLOW_CONGESTION: 2026-10-02: on the wide floorplan the initial global route of SA2 has 0 overflow, but the post-GRT design repair (3,400 buffers, 4,000 resized cells) re-routes incrementally and stopped with GRT-0232; with this flag the small overflow it creates is left to detailed routing, and signoff (DRC 0, LVS 0) decides whether the result is valid.
//GPL_CELL_PADDING: 2 = 1 site on each side (gpl.tcl / dpl_cell_pad.tcl halve the value with integer division, so 1 would mean no padding); 0 in the base. The detailed-routing hot spots of SA2 are 20-90 um clusters of fanout and max_cap buffers with large cells (buf_12, nor2_8); the core outside the macros is ~20 % used, so the padding costs no die area
//PL_TIME_DRIVEN: timing-driven global placement (off in the base): on 10.54 mm2 setup fell from +1.521 (placement estimate) to -1.287 ns (global-route estimate) on the half-cycle SRAM read path
//RT_CLOCK_MIN_LAYER: clock nets on met3-met5 (base: met1-met5): on 10.54 mm2 the level-1 clock net clknet_1_0_1_clk was routed ~4.9 mm for pins ~385 x 324 um apart (met1 869, met2 1,180 um), worst clock skew 0.737 -> 2.088 ns
//DRT_DRC_REPORT_ITER_STEP: reporting only: DRC report every 5 detailed-routing iterations, kept per routing call in drc_iter_<call>/
//RSZ_CORNERS: 2026-10-09: every resizer step (post-GPL / post-CTS / post-GRT repair, CTS, the post-route ECO) on the gated corners only. With the default (tt, ss, ff) and a 2.0 ns setup margin the resizer chased the ss corner, which no configuration closes at 20 ns (WNS -9 to -10 ns, about 7,600 endpoints): hours of buffering in the tag clusters; on DM_VC4 3400 the post-GRT timing repair alone raised the global-route overflow 66 -> 1,185 and left setup nom_tt -2.67 ns. ss stays reported in the sign-off STA (not gated). The SRAM macro .lib is kept by the first corner read, tt here (STA-1140).

//EXPERIMENT_SS: 2026-10-15 (owner: the rsztf sign-off is not accepted, ss far worse than R14). Measured on the signed 6c4ccffd layouts (results/ss_study_20261015): the ss loss sits in paths that are critical only at ss (DM: load data in W -> forwarding -> trap / stall cone into every pipeline register, max_ss -16.8 vs -7.1 on R14; SA2: if_req_addr -> I$ hit -> next-PC cone, -10.3 vs -7.0). With RSZ_CORNERS tt / ff no resizer step sees them. Change: PL_RESIZER_CORNERS = tt / ss / ff (local variable: the post-CTS timing repair alone also works on ss); every other resizer step stays on tt / ff, so the post-GRT repair still closes the tt paths (DM half-cycle RAM -> D$ refill).
//EXPERIMENT_SS_CELLS: 2026-10-15: the DM third ss step applied to SA2 (same method on every configuration): EXTRA_EXCLUDED_CELLS or4* / or3* (synthesis and PnR). The or3 / or4 families (NOR + inverter, 3-4 stacked PMOS) have the highest ss / tt delay ratio of the library (2.15-2.27, median 1.68; results/ss_study_20261015/lib_ss_tt_ratio_s0.2_l0.005.txt); on DM the change moved the ss proxy nom_ss from -8.96 to -7.13 ns (dm_grid3665x2900_rtl6c4c_rsztf_tdp_rszctsall_noor34_r1).
